statement: Whenever get_all_elements(root1, root2) returns a result r, r is exactly the nondecreasing sorted list of all node values of root1 and root2, with duplicates preserved. Equivalently: (a) len(r) = size(root1) + size(root2), where size(T) is the number of Node constructors in T; (b) for every i with 0 <= i < len(r) - 1, r[i] <= r[i+1]; and (c) for every integer v, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(r) and r[i] = v equals count_nodes(root1, v) + count_nodes(root2, v), where count_nodes(T, v) is the number of nodes of T whose value is v.
preconditions: root1 and root2 are binary search trees (for every node with value v, all values in its left subtree are <= v and all values in its right subtree are >= v); each tree contains between 0 and 5000 nodes; and every node value v satisfies -100000 <= v <= 100000.
